findings.title: Untested refusal when project is not header-safe
findings.problem: coworkFundingHeaders returns undefined when buildAttributionHeaders omits X-CodeMie-Project; no test covers this branch. All funding tests use header-safe project names (regression-gap).
findings.impact: If the check were dropped, a served session would declare codemie funding with no Project header and the backend could route by repository or default project; no existing test would fail. Reachability not confirmed against buildAttributionHeaders.
findings.recommendation: Add a forwarder test with a served, pinned Cowork session whose project is not header-safe, asserting no Routed-Via-CodeMie / Subscription-Type headers and fallback to the legacy path.

findings.title: Security sign-off for attribution headers missing
findings.problem: The change adds a new project-source derivation and a funding header set (coworkFundingHeaders, forwarder requestHeaders, pinAttribution) outside header-injection.plugin.ts; security-practices.md marks this CRITICAL and requires security-review sign-off. The task record says sign-off is required and records none.
findings.impact: The git-workflow Code Review Checklist blocks merge on attribution-header changes without this sign-off.
findings.recommendation: Record the security-review sign-off in the PR and task record and call the change out as CRITICAL in the PR description.

findings.title: Untested evidence/guard gate on funding headers
findings.problem: The `!req.evidence && !req.guard` condition on funding headers has no test for a session that is both recorded and Cowork-served/pinned; the native control is excluded by the missing mark instead.
findings.impact: Removing the condition would make recorded sessions declare CodeMie funding instead of answering to their record, and all current tests would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Add a forwarder test with a Cowork-served, pinned session that also has an evidence record or guard, asserting no Routed-Via-CodeMie or Subscription-Type: codemie headers.

findings.title: EPMCDME-17410 AC1 only partially met
findings.problem: Funding is declared only with a served mark and a pin source other than none. Sessions collected before marks/pins, spool-bound pre-pin sessions (pinned source none), and sessions whose identity resolution failed stay on the legacy Project header with subscription_type unknown; the pin is never rewritten. Tests encode this as intended.
findings.impact: The ticket AC says a Cowork session sent while connected to CodeMie has subscription_type codemie; these sessions never do, so their cost is not counted as CodeMie spend.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the AC accepts this boundary (document it and get the AC amended) or implement a funding path for these sessions, e.g. a safe upgrade of the pin source.
